text.p: These are the highlights in the Bosnian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The city council of Mostar, after nine months of delays, agreed to declare Mostar an "open city" which obliges council to allow for the return of refugees.

- The OSCE Election Appeals Sub-Commission rejected 3,270 registration applications in the Serb-controlled municipality of Brcko following an investigation which revealed local police and government authorities created and distributed bogus residency documents to potential voters.
- The Bosnian presidency on Tuesday did not reach an agreement on distribution of diplomatic and consulate missions among Moslems, Serbs and Croats.
- U.N. human rights envoy Elisabeth Rehn said after her visit to Mostar that she was encouraged with the announcement of the establishment of a unified police force for the Neretva canton.
- Bosnian federation president Vladimir Solijic was elected as president of executive committee of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna at its Monday session.

- Establishment of unified police in Mostar is an essential condition for ensuring freedom of movement not only for municipal elections in September but also for the peace process, OSCE official says.

- Former British foreign minister Douglas Hurd says in an inteview with Oslobodjenje that the crucial mistakes made by the international community during the Bosnian war were the creation of "protection zones" or safe areas and the establishment of the so-called double key mechanism for ordering NATO air strikes.

- Leaders from the opposition shadow government said they were deeply concerned that the OSCE had not set rules governing the campaign for local elections and had no clear strategy to implement poll results.
